title: Cannabis as a Plant: Origins, Uses, and Study
purpose: Establish a scientifically careful foundation for understanding Cannabis as a living plant, the limits of naming and origin claims, domestication and human selection, material identity, provenance, and responsible interpretation of evidence.
scopeNotes: Treat Cannabis sativa as a living vascular seed plant rather than beginning from consumer product categories.
Separate taxonomy, accession, line, clone, individual plant, organ, sample, cultivar, trade label, legal category, phenotype and chemotype.
Explain domestication and selection without overstating a single geographic-origin narrative.
Teach learners to evaluate ancestry, landrace, strain and provenance claims against the available evidence.
Separate plant-science conclusions from medical, legal and safety conclusions outside the resource scope.
Preserve uncertainty where evidence does not justify a stronger claim.

notes: Legacy package contains ten lessons, a 20-question final, practical, worksheet, glossary, instructor notes and visual briefs.
These components must be reviewed under the resource model; course-only assessment components should not automatically remain attached to the resource.
Known evidence verification remains incomplete for several references and must be closed before publication.
Legacy THC-C001 remains a permanent alias and historical identifier.
